subtitle: How the Gajapati standard rode the monsoon winds down the eastern coast

panels.shot: wide, stormy low-angle of a war elephant at a riverbank, banner whipping in monsoon wind
panels.action: Hamvira Deva stands on a towering war elephant by a broad southern river, armour glinting, as soldiers and campfires stretch behind him under dark, rain-heavy clouds.

dialogue.text: From Gauda’s marshes to the Krishna’s foam, Kapilendra and Hamvira drove Odisha’s banner south, carving an empire on a frontier where no border stayed still for long.

i18n.hi: गौड़ की दलदल से कृष्णा की लहरों तक, कपिलेंद्र और हमवीर ने ओडिशा का ध्वज दक्षिण धकेला, जहां सरहदें कभी टिकती ही नहीं थीं, वहां साम्राज्य तराशा।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a map spread on a dim royal chamber floor
panels.action: Hamvira Deva kneels over a painted palm-leaf map on a stone floor, tracing rivers with a dagger as lamplight flickers and courtiers’ shadows fall across the lines of the eastern coast.

dialogue.text: In the late 1440s, Kapilendra’s court at Cuttack whispered of seas and rivers, of Gauda in the north and rich deltas to the south, and of a prince named Hamvira who dared to link them.

i18n.hi: १५वीं सदी के आख़िर में, कटक दरबार में समंदर और नदियों की फुसफुसाहट थी—उत्तरी गौड़ की, दक्षिण के समृद्ध डेल्टा की, और उस राजकुमार हमवीर की जो इन्हें जोड़ने निकला था।

panels.shot: medium shot in royal audience hall, slightly low-angle on Hamvira before the throne
panels.action: In a pillared hall, Kapilendra’s unseen throne looms in shadow as Hamvira Deva stands before it, head bowed but eyes bright, hand resting on the hilt of his sword amid watching ministers.

dialogue.text: The Gajapati had already seized power in Odisha. Now, inscriptions show, he reached further: styling himself lord of Gauda and eyeing Rajamahendri and the Krishna beyond.

i18n.hi: गजपति ओडिशा पर तो काबिज़ हो ही चुका था। अब शिलालेख बताते हैं, उसने और बढ़कर खुद को गौड़ेश्वर कहा, नज़र राजमहेंद्री और आगे कृष्णा पर टिकी।

panels.shot: long coastal wide shot following marching columns along the shoreline
panels.action: Hamvira rides at the head of a long column of infantry, cavalry and elephants moving along a sandy coastline, with waves crashing to one side and rows of palm trees on the other.

dialogue.text: Hamvira’s task was simple to say and hard to keep: push the Gajapati standard down the eastern coast, while every village headman and frontier chief weighed which lord to serve.

i18n.hi: हमवीर का काम कहना आसान, निभाना मुश्किल: गजपति का ध्वज पूर्वी तट पर उतारते जाना, जबकि हर गांव-मुखिया और सरहद्दी सरदार सोचता रहा—किस राजा को मानूं?

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of elephants approaching a distant fortified town
panels.action: A fortified town with earthen walls and wooden towers rises above paddy fields as Hamvira’s elephants advance cautiously, archers and drummers forming ranks amid swirling dust.

dialogue.text: South lay Rajamahendri and the Godavari country, long fought over by Reddi chiefs and Vijayanagara officers. Kapilendra sent Hamvira to test their holds, fort by anxious fort.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण में था राजमहेंद्री और गोदावरी देश, जिसे रेड्डि नायकों और विजयनगर अफ़सरों ने बरसों बांटा था। कपिलेंद्र ने हमवीर को भेजा, कि हर बेचैन किले पर उनकी पकड़ आज़माए।

panels.shot: tight medium on Hamvira atop an elephant before city walls
panels.action: Hamvira stands on his elephant’s neck, arm raised in signal, as defenders watch from the battlements and smoke from burning outworks curls up into the sky.

dialogue.text: The records do not list every gate breached, every surrender signed, but they agree on one truth: by the mid-century, the Gajapati’s reach had gripped Rajamahendri and crossed the Krishna.

i18n.hi: हर टूटा फाटक, हर लिखी संधि का हिसाब नहीं, पर एक बात पर सब अभिलेख सहमत हैं: सदी के बीच तक गजपति की पकड़ राजमहेंद्री तक पहुंचकर कृष्णा को पार कर चुकी थी।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of a river crossing at dawn
panels.action: At dawn, mist hangs over the broad Krishna as Hamvira’s elephants wade through chest-deep water, soldiers balancing spears and bundles on their backs, the far bank just emerging in the haze.

dialogue.text: Somewhere along these sands, Gajapati standards first dipped in the Krishna’s current. Behind every crossing lay tribute wrung, alliances promised, and men who had thought the river a shield.

i18n.hi: कहीं इन्हीं रेतों पर पहली बार गजपति के ध्वज कृष्णा की धार में झुके। हर पार के पीछे था निचोड़ा हुआ नज़राना, किए हुए वादे, और वे जो नदी को ढाल समझ बैठे थे।

panels.shot: interior medium shot in a captured fort’s audience hall
panels.action: Inside a stone hall, Hamvira sits on a simple chair while a local chieftain in plain cotton bows, placing a small chest at his feet, as scribes sit cross-legged noting down terms.

dialogue.text: These wars were not only sieges. They were visits to halls like this, where local chiefs bargained for their seats, paid in cash, grain or elephants, and wondered how long this overlord would last.

i18n.hi: ये युद्ध सिर्फ घेराबंदी नहीं थे। ये ऐसे सभागृहों तक की यात्राएं भी थे, जहां स्थानीय नायक गद्दी पर सौदे करते, नक़द, अनाज या हाथी चढ़ाते, और सोचते—ये नया मालिक कब तक?

panels.shot: wide shot of Kondavidu hill-fort in the distance at sunset
panels.action: The massive hill-fort of Kondavidu, ringed with walls and bastions, rises over a rugged landscape as the sun sets red behind it, while Hamvira’s army camps in the valleys below.

dialogue.text: Beyond the Krishna stood Kondavidu, a hill-fort and symbol. The Matamuru inscription of Mallikarjuna, dated 1453, marks a time after which Vijayanagara’s hold here began to slip.

i18n.hi: कृष्णा के पार था कोंडविदु, पहाड़ी किला और प्रतीक। मल्लिकार्जुन के १४५३ के मतमूरु लेख के बाद से दिखता है कि यहां विजयनगर की पकड़ ढीली पड़ने लगी।

panels.shot: dynamic high-angle over siege works creeping up a hill
panels.action: From above, we see trenches, siege ramps and wooden towers creeping up Kondavidu’s slopes, with Hamvira on horseback overseeing engineers and soldiers hauling logs and stones.

dialogue.text: Later Odishan traditions remember Hamvira at Kondavidu. Modern historians read them alongside inscriptions, seeing not one clear conquest, but pressure that slowly turned a Vijayanagara bastion.

i18n.hi: ओडिशा की बाद की परंपराएं हमवीर को कोंडविदु पर याद रखती हैं। आधुनिक इतिहासकार इन्हें शिलालेखों से जोड़कर देखते हैं—स्पष्ट फतह नहीं, बल्कि वह दबाव जिसने धीरे-धीरे विजयनगर के गढ़ को मोड़ा।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Hamvira in a tense war-council tent
panels.action: Inside a canvas tent lit by oil lamps, Hamvira leans over a rough sketch of Kondavidu with his captains, his jaw set, as thunder rumbles outside and the tent walls tremble in the wind.

dialogue.speaker: kapilendra_deva_and_hamvira_deva
dialogue.text: Stone falls, but hill-forts also fall when the men within change masters.

i18n.hi: पत्थर गिरते हैं, और किले तब भी गिरते हैं जब अंदर के लोग मालिक बदल दें।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kondavidu gate opening to new banners
panels.action: A heavy wooden gate swings inward as weary defenders stand aside and Gajapati soldiers march in, hoisting their banner while some townsfolk watch from doorways with guarded faces.

dialogue.text: However Kondavidu changed hands—through siege, negotiation, or both—by the later 1450s Gajapati influence had reached its walls, and Kapilendra’s titles grew with every hill he could name.

i18n.hi: कोंडविदु चाहे घेराबंदी से बदला हो, चाहे समझौते से, या दोनों से—१४५० के दशक के अंत तक गजपति असर उसकी दीवारों तक पहुंच चुका था, और कपिलेंद्र की उपाधियां हर नई पहाड़ी से बढ़ती गईं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hamvira riding through a newly subjugated town
panels.action: Hamvira rides slowly through a narrow street of Kondavidu as shopkeepers stand aside, some bowing, some expressionless, while soldiers mark houses and granaries with chalk.

dialogue.text: New rulers meant new levies. Grain was counted, coins weighed, and men conscripted or disarmed. Glory at court meant, in the lanes, a careful weighing of how much the town could bear.

i18n.hi: नए शासक मतलब नए लगान। अनाज गिना गया, सिक्के तौले गए, और आदमी या तो भरती हुए या निहत्थे। दरबार की शान ने गलियों में यह सवाल छोड़ा—कितना बोझ शहर सह पाएगा?

panels.shot: wide shot of Devarakonda hill-fort with armies facing off in the plains below
panels.action: The steep, rocky hill of Devarakonda looms over a plain where two camps face each other—Hamvira’s on one side with elephants and standards, and another Deccan host on the other with horsemen and tents.

dialogue.text: Further west, inscriptions like the Veligalani plates and Chiruvrolu records remember Gajapati intervention at Mahur and Devarakonda, where local lords balanced Bahmani and Gajapati demands.

i18n.hi: और पश्चिम में, वेलिगलानि पट्टों और चिरुव्रोलु जैसे शिलालेख महूर और देवड़कोंडा में गजपति दख़ल को याद करते हैं, जहां स्थानीय नायक बहमनी और गजपति दोनों की मांगों को तोल रहे थे।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Hamvira and a Deccan commander in parley under a canopy
panels.action: Under a temporary canopy between the two camps, Hamvira faces a Deccan commander in rich robes, both standing stiffly as their retainers look on, hands near swords but faces deliberately calm.

dialogue.text: Sometimes, as the inscriptions suggest, the Gajapati prince did not stay to rule but came as an arbiter of force: to decide which chief kept his hill, which paid tribute, and which lost both.

i18n.hi: कभी-कभी, जैसा अभिलेख कहते हैं, गजपति राजकुमार राज करने नहीं, फ़ैसला करने आता था—किस नायक को पहाड़ रखना है, कौन सिर्फ नज़राना देगा, और किसे दोनों गंवाने हैं।

panels.shot: nighttime camp wide shot with storytellers around a fire
panels.action: At night in Hamvira’s camp, soldiers sit around a fire as a bard gestures dramatically, while elephants’ silhouettes loom and the distant outline of a hill-fort stands against the starry sky.

dialogue.text: In distant courts, Deccan chroniclers like those of the Burhan-i-Maasir and Tabaqat-i-Akbari wrote of vast Odishan hosts and endless elephants, numbers swollen by fear and rhetoric.

i18n.hi: दूर दरबारों में, बुरहान-ए-मासिर और तबक़ात-ए-अकबरी के लेखकों ने विशाल ओडिशा सेना और अंतहीन हाथियों के किस्से लिखे—संख्याएं डर और बयानबाज़ी से फूली हुई।

panels.shot: close-up on a Persian chronicler writing by lamplight, overlaid visually with a faint image of marching elephants
panels.action: A Persian chronicler sits cross-legged, pen poised over paper by lamplight, as faint, ghostly images of endless marching elephants seem to rise from the ink.

dialogue.text: Their pages show how the elephant-corps of Odisha were seen: not as a tally to be trusted, but as a looming edge of power at the frontier of Bahmani and Vijayanagara worlds.

i18n.hi: इन पन्नों में ओडिशा के हाथी-दल ऐसे दिखते हैं—गिनती पर नहीं, बल्कि ताक़त की धार की तरह, जो बहमनी और विजयनगर की दुनिया की सीमा पर मंडराती थी।

panels.shot: medium shot in Kapilendra’s court as a scribe reads out new royal titles
panels.action: Back in Cuttack, Hamvira stands to one side as a court scribe reads from a copper plate, while Kapilendra, seated on his throne, listens with a composed face and courtiers murmur.

dialogue.text: As campaigns piled up, so did names. In grants and plates, Kapilendra styled himself Gaudesvara, lord of Gauda, and Kalavargesvara, claiming authority across regions bound more by fear than maps.

i18n.hi: मुहिमें बढ़ती गईं, तो नाम भी। दान-पत्रों में कपिलेंद्र खुद को गौड़ेश्वर, यानी गौड़ का स्वामी, और कलवर्गेश्वर कहने लगा—ऐसे इलाकों पर दावा जिन्हें नक्शे से ज़्यादा डर ने बांध रखा था।

panels.shot: high-level wide shot of a patchwork frontier with different banners over forts
panels.action: From a bird’s-eye view, the land between Gauda and the Krishna appears as a patchwork: forts flying different banners, small camps on roads, and lines of border posts fading into the distance.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars see this not as a coloured map but a restless frontier, where Gajapati officers, Reddi houses, Vijayanagara commanders and Bahmani agents jostled in an ever-shifting web of loyalty.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान इसे रंगीन नक्शा नहीं, बेचैन सरहद देखते हैं—जहां गजपति अफ़सर, रेड्डि घराने, विजयनगर सेनापति और बहमनी कारिंदे वफादारी के बदलते जाल में भिड़ते रहे।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Hamvira alone, looking south from a rampart over rivers and plains
panels.action: Hamvira stands on a high rampart, helmet under his arm, gazing over rivers and fields stretching southward, his face thoughtful as storm clouds gather again on the horizon.

dialogue.speaker: kapilendra_deva_and_hamvira_deva
dialogue.text: We have reached the Krishna. But can a sword hold so many currents?

i18n.hi: हम कृष्णा तक आ चुके हैं। पर क्या तलवार इतनी धाराएं थाम सकती है?

panels.shot: final wide shot of the coastline from Gauda’s marshes to the Krishna delta at dawn
panels.action: At dawn, the camera glides along the eastern shoreline: mist over Gauda’s marshes, fishing boats near Rajamahendri, and at last the broad Krishna mouth, with scattered outposts flying Gajapati banners.

dialogue.text: For a brief span, Kapilendra and Hamvira stretched Odisha’s reach from Gauda to the Krishna, proving how far ambition and arms could go—and how expansion without firm borders could leave both glory and strain in its wake.

i18n.hi: थोड़े समय के लिए, कपिलेंद्र और हमवीर ने ओडिशा की पहुंच गौड़ से कृष्णा तक तान दी, दिखा दिया कि महत्वाकांक्षा और हथियार कहां तक जा सकते हैं—और कैसे बिना पक्की सरहदों के विस्तार, शान के साथ थकान भी छोड़ जाता है।

title_i18n.en: From Gauda to the Krishna River

subtitle_i18n.en: How the Gajapati standard rode the monsoon winds down the eastern coast
subtitle_i18n.hi: किस तरह गजपति का ध्वज मानसून संग पूर्वी तट पर उड़ा
